provenance.author: Jeffrey Flynt
provenance.acquisition: Manually transcribed field projection from GitHub connector; full raw-byte download unavailable in build environment.
provenance.transformation: Seed retains id, user, type, name, aliases, content, scope, status, pinned, supersession, resolution, edit flag, participants; missing optional fields normalized; cases omit description/notes; queries and assertions unchanged.
limitations: Not the full upstream benchmark protocol; single-turn assertions only; 12 session assertions are catalogued, not bundled.
Descriptions contain framework-specific assumptions; report is diagnostic, not a universal PA score.
One case contains no effective assertion and is explicitly unscored.
Original prose inconsistency "fails open (denies all)" is preserved; no correction made.

beliefs.content: Reads responses carefully rather than skimming. Prefers direct answers without lengthy preamble.
Wants explicit pushback when a plan has problems, rather than silent compliance.
Prefers a single strong recommendation over a menu of options.
Edits AI output rather than having AI edit their own drafts.
Writes TypeScript with strict mode and no implicit any.
Uses Fastify for HTTP services rather than Express.
Uses the MongoDB raw driver with explicit Collection types.
Prefers composition over inheritance. Factory functions returning plain objects rather than class hierarchies.
Go-style explicit error returns. Error tuples or Result<T> types rather than thrown exceptions.
Decided on MongoDB after evaluating Postgres. Raw driver only.
Previously used SQLAlchemy with Postgres. Stack replaced by MongoDB with raw driver.
Deploys services to a Kubernetes cluster on EKS. Uses Helm charts checked into the monorepo.
Frontend is React 18 with TanStack Query and Tailwind.
Evaluating JWT vs session tokens for the new auth service. Not decided.
Close third-person, present tense. No omniscient asides.
Previously wrote in first-person narrator voice. Replaced by close third-person.
Protagonist of the novel. Set in 1970s Lisbon. Does not reconcile with her father; ending is ambiguous.
Redis is a supporting character in the novel — a jazz pianist Mara meets in Lisbon.
Redis is used as a cache and rate-limiter in the backend. Single-node, not clustered.
Debating linear vs fragmented timeline for the novel.
Other user uses Haskell exclusively.
CI/CD runs on GitHub Actions. Merge to main triggers a deploy to staging; promotion to prod is manual.
Chapter 7 uses a deliberate POV shift to an unnamed observer. This is the only chapter that breaks close-third.
Was evaluating whether to self-host on bare metal or use Fly.io for the auth service.
Documentation prose should be terse and scannable. No marketing fluff.
Uses functional composition patterns with pipe() to chain data transformations instead of imperative loops.
Previously used TSLint for linting TypeScript. Replaced by ESLint.
Switched from TSLint to ESLint with @typescript-eslint. Later replaced by Biome.
Uses Biome for linting and formatting. Replaced ESLint and Prettier.
Uses Vitest for all testing. Replaced Jest.
Failed messages route to a MongoDB-backed dead letter queue with manual replay via admin CLI.
Deep React expertise — skip basics, engage on architecture and performance trade-offs.
Auth service depends on Redis for session storage. If Redis is down, auth fails open (denies all).
Was debating URL-path versioning vs header-based versioning for the public API.
Monorepo managed by Turborepo. Apps and packages in /apps and /packages directories.
